answer: Each identity must present a national ID attestation: a government-issued credential, verified by the issuing authority, bound to one person. A spiral winds inward to a single point, and an ID attestation does the same: one person, one identity, no branching. The velvet of a farm's IDs is smooth and new: all issued recently, all with similar numbers, all failing the authority's checks. A meadow of real identities is varied, with IDs from many years and many regions, and the network trusts only the attestations the authority itself confirms.
